headline: Washington's Air Attack Overwhelms Michigan State's Defense in Season Opener
body: Washington's passing game proved too much for Michigan State to contain in a 25-18 Week 1 victory that showcased the difference between two teams still finding their rhythm. Demond Williams Jr. carved up the Michigan State secondary with 265 passing yards and two touchdowns on 19 completions, establishing early command of the line of scrimmage that Michigan State's defense never managed to disrupt. The Spartans' pass rush, anchored by Schaffer's lone sack, couldn't generate consistent pressure, leaving Michigan State's secondary exposed to a methodical Washington attack that controlled the tempo.

Michigan State's passing game, meanwhile, stalled at 118 yards despite Glass completing 18 of 27 attempts with two touchdown passes. The Spartans' running game added only 97 yards on the ground, a combination that left the offense predictable and one-dimensional. Michigan State's two turnovers, both fumbles, came at inopportune moments and shifted field position in Washington's favor at critical junctures. The Spartans trailed 18-10 entering the fourth quarter and never found the offensive spark needed to climb back.

Washington's balanced attack—111 rushing yards paired with 256 passing yards—gave the coaching room multiple ways to attack. Bonner Jr. punched in a rushing touchdown while carrying the load with eight carries, and receiver Williams hauled in five catches for 95 yards to keep the chains moving. This was a dominant Week 1 performance that suggests Washington entered the season with a clearer offensive identity than Michigan State, which will need to address its communication and execution issues before next week's matchup.
turningPoint: Michigan State's second fumble in the fourth quarter gave Washington the ball in prime field position, leading directly to a score that put the game out of reach.

unsungHero.name: Karnley
unsungHero.why: Two sacks and four tackles in a disruptive defensive performance that set the tone for Washington's pass rush early, but gets overshadowed by Williams Jr.'s offensive showcase
